hooks.text: In 1983, Soviet satellites reported an incoming American nuclear strike.
Why did glinting sunlight on clouds almost trigger World War Three?
A Soviet warning system confirmed an incoming attack that never existed.

title: The Nuclear Alarm Caused by Sunlight on Clouds
description: In September 1983, a Soviet early-warning satellite detected incoming American nuclear missiles. Duty officer Stanislav Petrov realized the computer alert was a massive false alarm.

beats.text: In 1983, Soviet satellites reported an incoming American nuclear strike.
beats.visual: illustration of Soviet Oko nuclear early-warning satellite in Earth orbit, 1983

beats.text: On September 26, early-warning screens alerted duty officer Stanislav Petrov to five missiles.
beats.visual: portrait photograph of Soviet duty officer Stanislav Petrov in military uniform

beats.text: With impact minutes away, automated military computers registered the threat at highest reliability.
beats.visual: photograph of an American Minuteman ballistic missile launching from an underground silo

beats.text: Yet Petrov reasoned a real first strike would be an overwhelming barrage, not five isolated launches.
beats.visual: photograph of Stanislav Petrov seated at a military monitoring desk

beats.text: Ground radar showed clear skies over the horizon, confirming his suspicion.
beats.visual: photograph of a massive Cold War over-the-horizon radar installation antenna array

beats.text: Petrov decided against reporting an attack, notifying headquarters instead that the system had malfunctioned.
beats.visual: portrait photograph of Stanislav Petrov in front of military command monitors

beats.text: Investigations later revealed the satellite had encountered a rare orbital alignment with the Sun.
beats.visual: diagram illustrating the orbital path of a Soviet early-warning satellite relative to the Sun

beats.text: Sensors mistook bright reflection off high-altitude clouds for rocket flames.
beats.visual: satellite photograph of brilliant sunlight glinting off high-altitude Earth clouds from orbit

beats.text: Cloud-reflected sunlight nearly started World War Three.
beats.visual: portrait photograph of Stanislav Petrov in later years holding an award
